notes.text:
Precondition (2026-10-07): shell-write refusals recorded since 3.0.0 (tag v3.0.0 at 2026-09-18T00:42:55Z), sorted into covered / first-trivial / uncovered.
Command: python3 <scratchpad>/sort_shell_write_refusals.py <repo>/.claude/logs/plan-gate-events.jsonl (exit 0; read-only). Source: the dogfood checkout's plan-gate events feed, deny rows whose reason is one of the guard-secrets-read plan-gate write wordings. The redacted classifier corpus (quality-gates-internal .../classifier-events.redacted.jsonl) was read too: its guard-secrets-read rows carry no reason text and a truncated input, so a write cannot be told from a read there and none of its rows could be sorted; the result below rests on the events feed alone.
Rule: first-trivial = no earlier slot-taking row in the same session (allow.trivial, a require-plan slot-spent/second-file row, or an earlier shell-write refusal that would itself have taken the slot), so under one slot shared by both tools the write is allowed; uncovered = the slot was already spent, so Edit of the same file is graded by the tier too; covered = the pre-fix inline-eval wording that consulted no plan, so an Edit may have been covered (its row names no target).
Result: covered 1, first-trivial 2, uncovered 25, plus 4 rows outside the three words: targets carrying an expansion ($SP/..., $SCRATCH/..., $D/...) that the current guard already allows as unestablished destinations. Of the 25 uncovered, 22 compare against a slot or target the feed truncated to its first character (the heredoc wording is cut short), so a repeat of the slot's own file cannot be ruled out for them; 3 (session 82de1879) are distinct named files after the slot was spent.
Reading: the shared slot changes the verdict of the first-trivial rows only; every other recorded refusal is one an Edit of the same file would also have met at the deny tier.

Magnitude decision (decided 2026-10-06 by the orchestrator on the operator's standing instruction; recorded 2026-10-07 as this task's basis): a shell write whose magnitude the command does not state takes the session's first-trivial slot exactly as an Edit within trivialLineThreshold would, because PreToolUse cannot see the change before it happens. The PostToolUse arm (guard-bash-writes), which does see the change, reports it when it exceeded trivialLineThreshold. So the PreToolUse verdict is the same whichever tool makes the change, and an oversized shell write is reported after the fact rather than guessed at beforehand.

Correction to the magnitude decision note (2026-10-07, after review round 2): the PostToolUse report of an oversized shell write that took the slot is NOT built by this task. Its builder is P108.7-4gh (guard-bash-writes reports an oversized shell write after the fact), which depends on this task. Until P108.7-4gh lands, an unstated oversized shell write that took the slot is reported by nothing, and the docstrings this task wrote say exactly that. "Decided by the orchestrator on the operator's standing instruction" refers to the operator's 2026-10-06 instruction adopting every proposal in this plan and asking for the run to go to completion without waiting. The decision stays open to the operator's review at phase sign-off.

tasks.title: a secret path inside a string literal is not a read
tasks.description: Fix BUG-19-4gh: guard-secrets-read refuses a program fed to an interpreter's stdin whose only reference to a secret file is a string literal (python3 - <<'PY' DOC = "the guard refuses open('.env') in a program"; print(len(DOC)) PY) - the guard matches the program's text, not an operation it performs. Decided 2026-10-06: that program is allowed. A secret path that appears only inside a string literal that is not the argument of a read call is not a read; a program that passes such a literal to open(), read_text(), or a subprocess that reads it is still refused, and so is every shape the guard refuses today outside string literals. test_hooks.py's g06 loses its known-divergence mark. This is guard-reading code: if a model or classifier safeguard stops the attempt, the refusal is recorded verbatim with audit-task note and the task is handed to the human; nobody rewords the work to get past it.

tasks.title: a write inside a subshell or command substitution is graded like the same write outside it
tasks.description: Fix BUG-20-4gh. guard-secrets-read's shell-write reader must descend into subshell `( ... )` and command-substitution `$( ... )` (and backtick) bodies, so a redirect, `tee`, `sed -i` or interpreter write inside one is graded exactly like the same write outside it. Reuse the shared shell readers in hooks/_config (command_clauses / split_heredocs) rather than adding a second grammar. If a form stays unreadable, it is named in the guard's own list of what it cannot see. Cases: each form alone at every tier; each after an interpreter write in the same command (the second file is graded and the slot is spent at most once); and allow twins: a read-only subshell such as `(cd src && ls)`, and a substitution that only reads, such as `x=$(cat README.md)`.
